newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: KL small-caps end barely up, blue chips slip.
newsitem.headline: KL small-caps end barely up, blue chips slip.

text.p: Lured by fat gains on the lofty Kuala Lumpur small-capitalisation sector, investors locked in profits by day's end, but the Second Board index managed to claw its way into the plus column.

Blue chips finished lower, with the Composite Index slipping 2.79 points to 1,123.72. The Second Board began the day higher but lost steam by midday. It regained some composure at the close to end up 0.31 points to 608.79.
The U.S. Federal Reserve Open Market Committee meets on Tuesday to discuss interest rate policy. Analysts anticipate the central bank may boost rates by 25 basis points.

"There's been a lack of participation in the market due to the FOMC," said Laurence Lau, director of research at Jupiter Securities. "Above 600 (on the Second Board index), people would take a chance to slow things down a bit."
A dealer at a local firm said, "It's about time that there should be consolidation on the Second Board."
Volume thinned considerably to 258 million shares from over 320 million on Monday. Losers outpaced gainers by 383 to 170 with 160 counters unchanged.
Technology Resources Industries (TRI) continued to lead the actives list, off 10 cents to 6.10 ringgit.
